item.title: Can the Monarchy Survive the Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor Scandal?
item.description: “The longer it goes on, the more damaging it will be for the institution,” royals historian Ed Owens tells Vanity Fair of what he calls “the biggest crisis since the abdication of Edward VIII in 1936.”

item.title: Kelly Klein: The Muse Who Shaped '90s Fashion With Her Friend Carolyn Bessette Kennedy
item.description: Twenty years after divorcing Calvin Klein, Kelly Klein is getting another turn in the spotlight thanks to her character being on American Love Story.

item.title: Trump’s State of the Union: Hockey Champions and Grisly Tales of Bloodshed
item.description: In the longest ever State of the Union address, President Trump camouflaged his claims of a historic economic boom in star-spangled spectacle as his approval ratings dip deep underwater.

item.title: Robyn Says Sexistential “Is Not a Self-Help Album”
item.description: Robyn was tired of feeling like “a lonely cowboy” when she made Honey. Then she started writing Sexistential and found herself heartbroken once again. Here, she tells VF about embracing both heartbreak and horniness in equal measure, and starring in a new campaign with Swedish label Acne Studios.

item.title: What Stellan Skarsgård Really Thinks About: Fashion Shows, Press Tours, His Sentimental Value Co-Stars
item.description: “I mean, my 13 year old boy likes it, and thinks it’s not slow, and he thinks that a TikTok is slow!” Stellan Skarsgård tells VF about Sentimental Value, in which he stars alongside Elle Fanning and Renate Reinsve, “it’s a film that gets all people.”

item.title: A Tour of Tracee Ellis Ross's Effortlessly Cool Office in West Hollywood
item.description: The Blackish star is officially in her beauty-mogul era with her natural hair care brand, Pattern Beauty. But her corporate life is anything but drab.

item.title: ‘Grey Gardens’ at 50: Were Little Edie and Big Edie Exploited, or In On the Fun?
item.description: Is the canonical documentary about Bouvier relatives “Big” and “Little” Edie Beale an exploitative farce, a second-wave feminist masterpiece, or somehow both at the same time?

item.title: Is Paul McCarthy the Most Dangerous Artist in LA?
item.description: In a wide-ranging interview, the artist talks to Vanity Fair about his first hometown show in years, the fires that destroyed his home and studio, and how artists can make vital, trenchant work about the political discourse—even if it pisses off the collectors.

item.title: Meghan Markle and Prince Harry Make a Semi-Official Trip to Jordan to Visit José Andrés
item.description: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have landed in Amman to meet the WHO and World Central Kitchen projects with which they collaborate in Jordan.

item.title: Long Live The King! Baz Luhrmann and Vanity Fair Host a Snowy, Society-Heavy Screening of EPiC: Elvis Presley in Concert
item.description: Luhrmann unearthed hours of footage of Elvis on stage, and gave an early look to a crowd at the Crosby Street Hotel.
